Additional handlers under review include UpdateMemo, DeleteMemo, SetMemoAttachments, SetMemoRelations, and reaction handlers. CreateMemoComment may transitively call CreateMemo, which dispatches a created webhook.

CreateMemo, UpdateMemo, and DeleteMemo each route through dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook to PostAsync. CreateMemoComment routes through DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook to PostAsync, and also transitively triggers CreateMemo's created webhook. SetMemoAttachments follows the same dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects path.

SetMemoRelations also routes through dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects. The single function where these paths converge before delivery is webhook.PostAsync. All memo-related handlers—CreateMemo, UpdateMemo, DeleteMemo, SetMemoAttachments, SetMemoRelations, and CreateMemoComment—eventually reach this function before the actual delivery occurs.

OAuth IDP handlers such as CreateSession may also trigger outbound requests to user-configured token URLs. The question’s phrasing about “user-configured URL” and “converge before delivery” aligns with webhook dispatch patterns.

Checking DeleteMemo and reaction handlers for webhook dispatches. IDP SSO handlers may reach user-configured URLs directly without passing through webhook.PostAsync.

CreateMemo, UpdateMemo, DeleteMemo, CreateMemoComment, SetMemoAttachments, and SetMemoRelations are the RPC handlers. They converge at webhook.PostAsync in internal/webhook/webhook.go. PostAsync is the correct convergence point because Post itself is delivery.

GetHTMLMeta and OAuth ExchangeToken are additional RPC handlers that may trigger outbound HTTP requests to user-configured URLs. The next step is identifying the single convergence function where these paths merge before delivery.

Webhooks appear to be the clearest user-configured URL path. Link metadata and OAuth likely diverge into separate functions, so they probably do not converge to a single delivery point.

The three RPC handlers are CreateMemo, UpdateMemo, and DeleteMemo. They converge at webhook.PostAsync in internal/webhook/webhook.go. Comment changes route through dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook instead.

The full answer includes CreateMemoComment, SetMemoAttachments, and SetMemoRelations as the three RPC handlers. All six converge at PostAsync in internal/webhook/webhook.go.

`CreateMemo`, `UpdateMemo`, `DeleteMemo`, `CreateMemoComment`, `SetMemoAttachments`, `SetMemoRelations`; `PostAsync` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`

Those RPC handlers dispatch memo webhooks (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, `memo_service_comments.go`, `memo_attachment_service.go`, `memo_relation_service.go`). All of them end in `webhook.PostAsync`, which queues the POST to the user-configured URL; workers then call `Post` for the actual request.
